title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

errors: The exactness of the columns on the left (injectivity of π_1(X,x) into π_1 of the universal curve) is used without comment. It holds for hyperbolic (g,ν), where 2g−2+ν>0: the geometric fundamental group is centre-free, and one has the profinite Birman sequence and homotopy exact sequence for the curve fibration. But it needs that hyperbolicity hypothesis and a stack-theoretic π_1, neither of which is stated.
M_{g,ν} and 𝔛_{g,ν} are stacks (or require level structure), so π_1 must be taken in the stack or orbifold sense. This is implicit.
Notation slip: the standard objects reuse the letters M_{g,ν}, N_{g,ν} both for the stacks and for their arithmetic fundamental groups.
The Galois quotient is Γ_{Q̃/Q} with Q̃ the algebraic closure of Q in k, not literally Γ_{Q̄/Q}. This is fine since Q̃ ≅ Q̄ non-canonically.

ideas.what: Arithmetic fundamental group of the moduli stack M_{g,ν} over Q as an extension of Gal(Q̄/Q) by the profinite mapping class group
ideas.modern_name: Outer Galois action on profinite mapping class groups / arithmetic Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); developed by Ihara, Oda (1990s), Nakamura, Matsumoto
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2–§3 on the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: 3×3 diagram combining the profinite Birman sequence (universal curve over moduli) with the geometric/arithmetic sequences
ideas.modern_name: Profinite Birman exact sequence plus homotopy exact sequence for M_{g,ν+1} → M_{g,ν} over Q
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA1 XIII (homotopy exact sequence); Asada, Nakamura, Matsumoto (profinite Birman / Galois version)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. XIII gives the homotopy exact sequence; the moduli version is not in published Grothendieck texts as such

ideas.what: Comparing fundamental groups at arbitrary base points over algebraically closed k with standard complex ones via non-canonical isomorphisms (to become path torsors on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Étale path torsors / fundamental groupoid, comparison with transcendental base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 fundamental groupoid); Deligne 1989 (tangential base points)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V; Esquisse d'un programme

deep.surprise_reason: This is a recap of standard (to Grothendieck and later to the anabelian school) fundamental-group bookkeeping for the Teichmüller tower. The more interesting conjecture, that P^φ determines φ, sits on the previous page.
transcription_corrections: Galois groups in diagram (1) are written Γ_{Q̃/Q} (tilde), consistent with the marginal note 'Q̃ = la clôture alg. de Q dans k', not Γ_{Q̄/Q}.
First line: 'k corps alg. clos, car. 0', i.e. algebraically closed of characteristic 0.
'un fibration de [?]' is likely 'une fibration de champs' or similar; the reading is uncertain.
The group written 𝔊_{X,x} is the same symbol (sigma-like) transcribed 𝔖 on the next page.
In the definitions (2), M_{X,x} and N_X are π_1 of 𝔛_{g,ν} and M_{g,ν} without subscript k, i.e. over Q.
